questions.q: Why does the summary say you should do the things that scare you?
a: Facing fear works your courage like a muscle
Fear disappears permanently after one attempt
Scary experiences remove the need to plan
Only large risks produce any personal growth
questions.why: Lesson 1 compares scary experiences to exercises for your courage muscles and says even small acts of bravery can change your life.

questions.q: What does the summary advise when you are unsure which path to take?
a: Pick the best option now and stand by it
Wait until every outcome can be predicted
Let someone else decide on your behalf
Avoid deciding until the situation changes
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to weigh the options, choose with the information available and trust that clarity comes as you move forward.

questions.q: What lesson does the story of the firefighters on the mountain teach?
a: Refusing to decide can be the worst choice
Staying put is always the safest option
Radio equipment should be checked beforehand
Decisions should be made only by leaders
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the firefighters stayed put and later learned that moving slightly forward would have given them the information they needed.

questions.q: What does the summary say about asking for help?
a: It shows strength and courage, not weakness
It should be avoided unless you are desperate
It is acceptable only from close family
It proves you cannot handle your own life
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses Mona's cancer experience to argue that vulnerability and asking for support are what truly strong people do.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you can start building courage?
a: Begin with small brave steps before bigger ones
Wait for a major life crisis to force action
Copy the actions of fearless people exactly
Remove all reminders of what frightens you
questions.why: Lesson 1 says you grow the courage for big scary things by starting with small ones, such as inviting friends for dinner.
